Thanks — adding the engineering POV below. Long form so Applify has something to reference for the SOW.

1) Baseline sizing guidance (first 30 days)- Model: LLM ensembles vary; if Applify plans to run a mix of 7B and 13B models, A10G or A40-equivalent (16GB+) are a good starting point. If strictly 13B and quantized to 4-bit, 48GB cards (e.g., H100/80GB alternatives) reduce node count but increase cost.
- Starting pool recommendation: 8 nodes (A10G equiv) – expected steady concurrent requests ~40 inference streams, p50 latency target < 200ms for short-form prompts.

2) Autoscaling & burst policy (recommended)- Autoscaler rules: scale up when avg GPU util > 60% for 60s; scale down when avg GPU util < 30% for 300s.- Min/Target/Max = 6 / 8 / 20.- Burst reserve: keep a warm standby of 2 nodes (hot-warmed, preloaded model weights) and allow ephemeral burst instances (cold-started) up to +12 nodes with a ~2–5 minute provisioning window.- Cost control: enforce a budget cap and automatic fallback to a lower-cost quantized model variant when burst budget > 60% of monthly allocation.

3) Regional capacity considerations- Preferred: us-west-2 for latency to Applify HQ. We should reserve quota there early; alternative region us-east-1 for cross-region failover.

4) Operational notes- KV caching: recommend enabling prefix caching for heavy-reuse paths to cut token compute by ~25%.- Canary/rollout: start with 10% traffic on dedicated pool, gradual ramp over 3 days.

5) Timeline and prerequisites- Provisioning lead time (reserve capacity): 5–10 business days once PO and sizing approved.- Network: VPC peering + 1 static NAT IP for callbacks. KMS access for customer keys required before production.

I'll add these items into the provisioning-template.json and push to the shared Confluence page.

-Rishi
